sourcePolicy: Use public lexical sources as corroborating evidence, not as self-approving production data.
Preserve the pinned STEPBible/TBESG/TFLSJ source lock from the Luke v4 track as the canonical source family; public web-accessible mirrors are intake corroboration only.
Do not flatten classical/full-lexicon extensions into Luke-specific meanings without exact Luke context support.
Morphology and token counts constrain usage but are not independent lexical senses.

sources.note: STEP Bible public Strong view confirms agapao and Luke uses including Luke 6:27, 6:32 and 6:35.
Public BibleCrawler lexical/morphology view gives G0021 agalliao: be delighted, have joy, exult, be glad, rejoice; full-lexicon note marks the stronger exult/rejoice boundary.
Public Strong/TBESG/Abbott-Smith aggregation gives aganakteo: be indignant, very displeased; explicitly cites Luke 13:14.
Public lexical views corroborate agapao=to love; agape=love/goodwill/esteem; agapetos=beloved/dear; angelos=messenger/angel with NT angel sense.
Public TBESG/Abbott-Smith aggregation gives agele=herd and explicitly cites Luke 8:32-33.
Public TBESG/Abbott-Smith aggregation gives hagiazo: make holy, consecrate, sanctify, set apart; the 'treat as holy' sense explicitly cites Luke 11:2.

targets.lexicalIntake: Public lexical evidence supports rejoice/exult/be glad with stronger joy intensity than a neutral pleasure gloss.
Public TBESG/Abbott-Smith evidence explicitly ties Luke 13:14 to indignation/strong displeasure.
STEP and public lexica support love/esteem/goodwill across persons and things. Luke-specific context must prevent importing a simplistic agapao-vs-phileo theological dichotomy as a lexical rule.

Public Abbott-Smith evidence supports love/goodwill/esteem. Luke 11:42 requires context-specific review of 'the love of God' without turning lexical meaning into a full systematic-theology definition.
Public full-lexicon evidence gives beloved/dear while preserving older classical extensions; Luke use should prioritize the personal 'beloved' sense.

Public lexical evidence preserves the broader messenger/envoy sense and the biblical angel sense. Exact Luke contexts must decide whether each token is heavenly angel or human messenger rather than flattening all tokens to one gloss.
Public TBESG/Abbott-Smith evidence gives herd and explicitly cites Luke 8:32-33.

Public TBESG/Abbott-Smith evidence distinguishes make/consecrate/sanctify from 'treat as holy'; Luke 11:2 is explicitly cited under the latter boundary, so hallow/regard as holy must be tested before importing broader sanctification senses.
